acceptance_criteria.description: Default Windows process adapter selects a real package-portable Job Object backend and reports supported only after a successful native capability probe with killOnClose=true.

Managed launch establishes the Job boundary before descendant escape, verifies the expected process creation identity, and retains opaque handle-bound custody through inspect, graceful/escalated termination, and release.

Termination and controller-loss cleanup act through the Job handle, converge for the entire owned process family, do not target a PID-reused replacement, and fail closed/retryably on malformed protocol, helper loss, identity mismatch, or unavailable native APIs.
The raw-PID validated-tree fallback cannot yield a supported release-grade Windows custody capability or proof; unrelated processes and Linux custody behavior remain unchanged.
Focused unit/platform/release checks, build, and Windows structural/native proof pass; docs accurately state portability, identity, helper lifecycle, failure modes, and support boundaries.

closed_decisions: Supported Windows managed launch must use a real Job Object whose native handle remains live for custody and whose limits include kill-on-close; the package must not depend on an external unpublished binary, absolute development path, ambient checkout, or runtime download.

Custody must be established before the launched application can create descendants outside the Job. A post-launch open-by-PID assignment alone is insufficient unless the implementation proves an equivalent no-escape launch barrier.

The backend must bind the opened/launched process to the expected creation identity before destructive authority exists, and termination must use the retained Job handle rather than taskkill or another raw PID command.

A helper or bridge that owns the Job handle must fail closed, use bounded framed communication, sanitize errors/evidence, close the Job on controller loss, and leave no independently long-lived helper after normal cleanup.

If the native Job backend is unavailable, capability and cleanup evidence must report Windows custody unavailable/non-release-grade. The windows_validated_tree raw-PID path may remain only as non-authoritative diagnostics or emergency best effort and must not satisfy supported release criteria.
Linux process-group behavior and existing identity/nonce/lease checks must remain intact. No new third-party runtime dependency or lockfile change is authorized.

focused: pnpm vitest run tests/unit/windows-job-object.test.ts tests/unit/windows-custody.test.ts tests/unit/windows-process.test.ts tests/unit/process-custody.test.ts tests/unit/session-manager.test.ts tests/unit/session-recovery.test.ts tests/platform/ownership-proof.test.ts tests/platform/background-proof.test.ts tests/release/release-safety.test.ts
natural: On a Windows host, run the repository's bounded native Job Object proof without launching or terminating unrelated processes.

forbidden_changes: Do not edit public MCP/dialog behavior, provider source or delivery, artifacts/observability beyond custody evidence compatibility, dependencies/lockfiles, queue/blocker/release files, git, Jira, or pull requests.
Do not claim a raw-PID revalidation followed by taskkill is identity-bound or release-grade.

Do not allow a launched child to run before the Job boundary is established, silently fall back after Job setup failure, use shell interpolation, accept unbounded helper output, expose raw command lines/nonces/paths in public evidence, or kill by PID after identity uncertainty.
Do not download or compile an ambient native dependency at package runtime.
objective: Complete the Windows Job Object custody seam with a package-portable native backend that binds custody to the launched process identity before descendant escape, terminates through the held Job handle, and removes the raw-PID validated-tree fallback from release-grade support claims.
